claims.text: The as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy lacks a controlled nanoprecipitate dispersion.
An optimized heat treatment can trigger precipitation of nanometer-scale coherent secondary phases in the eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Tuning heat-treatment temperature, time, and cooling rate can produce a uniform dispersion of coherent nanoprecipitates without over-aging.
Atmospheric control during heat treatment prevents oxidation.
Atmospheric control during heat treatment maintains alloy purity.
Coherent nanoprecipitates act as dislocation-pinning centers.
Coherent nanoprecipitates produce local stress fields.
Dislocation pinning and precipitate-associated stress fields impede dislocation motion and thereby increase strength.
The nanoprecipitates promote dislocation multiplication and activation of additional slip systems.
Additional dislocation activity and slip-system activation enhance ductility.
A sufficiently fine and well-distributed precipitate population prevents brittle failure while accommodating plastic deformation.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the heat-treated alloy will have higher yield strength.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the heat-treated alloy will have higher ultimate tensile strength.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, the heat-treated alloy will have greater elongation at fracture.
Overly aggressive heat treatment can cause precipitate over-aging or coarsening.
Precipitate over-aging or coarsening can reduce both strength and ductility.
Ductility enhancement from precipitation has been observed in multiphase alloys.
Direct evidence for the proposed simultaneous improvement in eutectic high-entropy alloys is limited.
The hypothesis is falsified if treatment fails to produce a statistically significant improvement in both strength and ductility relative to the as-cast control.
The hypothesis is falsified if the expected coherent nanoprecipitates are not observed.
